children: Gimlet Labs, a research lab building AI infrastructure, said on Friday it raised $300 million in a funding round that valued the company at $3 billion, as investors continue to back companies building the infrastructure underpinning AI.

Investor capital has increasingly flowed into AI and related infrastructure driving a surge in billion-dollar startups, rapid fundraising rounds and soaring valuations for a select group of fast-growing companies.
The Series B funding round was led by Andreessen Horowitz, with participation from Sapphire Ventures, Microsoft's venture fund M12, Arm, and existing investors Menlo Ventures and Factory.
Gimlet Labs builds infrastructure for running AI agents across different types of computing hardware.

The company emerged from stealth in October 2025, betting that growing adoption of agentic AI will drive demand for its multi-silicon software platform, which helps customers manage AI workloads more efficiently.
The San Francisco, California-based company said the new funding will be used to expand operations for its multi-silicon cloud platform and grow its team.
